jurisdiction.name: Venezuela
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Venezuela has no AI law and no data protection law. At the highest level, the Organic Law on the Homeland Plan 2025-2031, published in May 2025, includes a state policy line on artificial intelligence calling for ethical and responsible AI development, regulatory frameworks and ethical principles, and protection against algorithmic bias. The science and technology ministry (MINCYT) leads AI policy and in February 2026 presented a non-binding Code of Ethics for the Responsible Development and Application of AI. An AI bill has been pending since its first discussion in November 2024, and a National AI Plan has been announced, but no plan document was found.
lead_institutions: Ministerio del Poder Popular para Ciencia y Tecnología (MINCYT)
narrative.review_notes: Reviewed again on 18 October 2026: the official gazette, the National Assembly, the science and technology ministry, the central bank, the telecommunications regulator and the electronic certification authority were checked, and the 2025-2031 Homeland Plan with its AI policy line was added. The AI bill's text is still not public on the National Assembly's site. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the banking regulator, the education ministry, the standards body and the national IT centre. The AI bill, the National AI Plan and the cybersecurity and digital rights bills remain pending.

instruments.official_title: Código de Ética para el Desarrollo y Aplicación Responsable de la Inteligencia Artificial
instruments.english_title: Code of Ethics for the Responsible Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Popular Power for Science and Technology (MINCYT), General Directorate for the Development and Application of Artificial Intelligence (DGDAIA), Vice-Ministry for the Development of Information and Communication Technologies
instruments.current_status: Presented by the Minister of Science and Technology on 19 February 2026 and treated as non-binding ministerial guidance: the document carries no date, resolution number or Gaceta Oficial reference, and no Gaceta publication was found. MINCYT describes it as one of three pillars alongside the pending AI bill and a National AI Plan.
instruments.summary: Ethics code drafted by MINCYT's General Directorate for the Development and Application of AI that sets nine guiding principles for AI in Venezuela: humanist AI, equity and non-discrimination, environmental responsibility, security, privacy, transparency, accountability, open science and excellence. It addresses everyone involved in AI research, development, innovation and application, and AI users, and expects among other things consent for data use by AI systems, auditable and explainable models, human oversight with final human responsibility, and avoidance of mass surveillance, manipulation and profiling that segments people. It also reviews the national legal framework (Constitution, Science, Technology and Innovation Law, Infogobierno Law) and international references such as the UNESCO Recommendation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Venezuela's only published national AI-specific governance document; the reference ethical framework pending an AI law.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Popular Power for Science and Technology

instruments.official_title: Ley Orgánica del Plan de la Patria de las 7 Grandes Transformaciones 2025-2031
instruments.english_title: Organic Law on the Homeland Plan of the 7 Great Transformations 2025-2031
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly (promulgated by the President of the Republic)
instruments.current_status: The national development plan for 2025-2031, approved by the National Assembly as an organic law and published in Official Gazette No. 6.907 Extraordinary of 24 May 2025, promulgated the same day. Its AI line sets direction only; it does not itself regulate AI.
instruments.summary: Venezuela's national development plan for 2025-2031, organised around seven 'great transformations'. Under the science and technology transformation, strategic line 6.2.4.4 sets a state policy on the impact of artificial intelligence: developing AI research and adoption with ethical and responsible use, centres of excellence and specialised talent, and establishing regulatory frameworks and ethical principles for transparent, equitable and safe AI that protect citizens' rights and limit risks such as algorithmic bias and discrimination. The plan also calls for strengthening national cybersecurity and promoting a digital, cybersecurity and AI strategy through international partnerships.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Highest-level national plan with an explicit AI policy line; it frames the later AI ethics code, the AI bill and the National AI Plan.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Venezuela's official gazette, the National Assembly's law listings, the science and technology ministry, the central bank, the telecommunications regulator and the electronic certification authority were searched. Apart from the 2025-2031 Homeland Plan's AI policy line and the AI ethics code, no qualifying AI-governance document was found, and there is no data protection law. The AI bill, the National AI Plan and the cybersecurity and digital rights bills are listed under Leads until their texts are published.

The Supreme Court's gazette portal, the National Printing Office, the central bank and the National Assembly's bill pages could not be accessed, so the AI bill's text and status could not be read; the official gazette's own search was used instead. Venezuela is marked for a later retry and, as a country of over 20 million people with few records, for a longer catch-up pass. The AI bill, the National AI Plan and new AI vice-ministries are tracked as leads.

leads.title: Proyecto de Ley de Inteligencia Artificial
leads.note: Pending bill. Approved at first discussion on 19 November 2024 (date stated in MINCYT's AI ethics code, p. 7). Reported by MINCYT on 8 January 2026 as still under debate in the National Assembly; on 16 April 2026 MINCYT announced a 'Ley Nacional para el Desarrollo y Uso Ético de la Inteligencia Artificial' would be submitted to the Assembly (https://mincyt.gob.ve/mincyt-impulsa-seis-proyectos-de-ley-estrategicos-para-fortalecer-la-ciencia-tecnologia-y-transformacion-digital-de-venezuela/). No bill text on asambleanacional.gob.ve (bill pages and searches not public / blocked) and no sanction in the Gaceta Oficial found as of 12 October 2026. Record once sanctioned and published. 2026-10-18: the National Assembly's bill listing opened, but the AI bill's page still shows that the project is no longer public and the site's search and further listing pages are refused; no sanction found in the Official Gazette text search.
